Hodrick-Prescott filter with a fixed smoothing parameter

Source: R/filters.R
hp_filter.Rd

hp_filter() splits a time series into a smooth trend and a cycle with the filter of Hodrick and Prescott (1997) and a smoothing parameter \(\lambda\) chosen by the user: 1600 for quarterly data, 100 for annual data and 129600 for monthly data are the conventional values (Ravn and Uhlig 2002).

Usage

hp_filter(x, lambda = 1600, as_dt = TRUE, log_scale = FALSE)

# Default S3 method
hp_filter(x, lambda = 1600, as_dt = TRUE, log_scale = FALSE)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector or a ts object, without missing values; at least 5 observations.

lambda

the smoothing parameter \(\lambda > 0\) (default 1600, for quarterly data).

as_dt

TRUE (default) returns a data.table; FALSE a list.

log_scale

filter the logarithm of the series (default FALSE, as in version 0.1.0).

Value

With as_dt = TRUE, a data.table with the columns original, trend, cycle (and time for a ts) and the attribute lambda. With as_dt = FALSE, a list of class c("mhp_hp", "mhp", "mhp_result", "list") with original, trend, cycle, lambda, then log_scale, trend_log and cycle_log (with log_scale = TRUE) and time and frequency (for a ts). Methods: print(), plot(), ggplot2::autoplot(), mhp_interpret().

Details

The trend \(\mathbf{g} = (g_1, \dots, g_T)^\top\) of the series \(\mathbf{x}\) minimises $$\sum_{t=1}^{T}(x_t - g_t)^2 + \lambda\sum_{t=2}^{T-1}\left[(g_{t+1} - g_t) - (g_t - g_{t-1})\right]^2,$$ so that \(\hat{\mathbf{g}} = (\mathbf{I} + \lambda\mathbf{A})^{-1}\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{B}\mathbf{x}\) with \(\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{K}^\top\mathbf{K}\) and \(\mathbf{K}\) the \((T - 2) \times T\) matrix of second differences (rows \((1, -2, 1)\)). The cycle is \(\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{g}}\). The system is pentadiagonal, symmetric and positive definite and is solved in \(O(T)\) operations.

With log_scale = TRUE the filter is applied to \(\log x_t\); the trend is returned as \(\exp(\hat{g}_t)\) and the cycle as \(x_t - \exp(\hat{g}_t)\), and the components on the log scale are added to the list result.

References

Hodrick, R. J. and Prescott, E. C. (1997). Postwar U.S. business cycles: an empirical investigation. Journal of Money, Credit and Banking, 29(1), 1–16. doi:10.2307/2953682

Ravn, M. O. and Uhlig, H. (2002). On adjusting the Hodrick-Prescott filter for the frequency of observations. The Review of Economics and Statistics, 84(2), 371–376. doi:10.1162/003465302317411604

See also

mhp_filter, fmhp_filter, mhp_compare

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(us_macro)
gdp <- ts(data = us_macro$gdp, start = c(1959, 1), frequency = 4)
hp <-
  hp_filter(
      x         = log(gdp)
    , lambda    = 1600
    , as_dt     = TRUE
    , log_scale = FALSE
    )
hp
#>      original    trend        cycle    time
#>         <num>    <num>        <num>   <num>
#>   1: 7.904833 7.896154  0.008678366 1959.00
#>   2: 7.929775 7.905529  0.024246310 1959.25
#>   3: 7.928582 7.914908  0.013673747 1959.50
#>   4: 7.932076 7.924314  0.007762667 1959.75
#>   5: 7.954267 7.933774  0.020492108 1960.00
#>  ---                                       
#> 199: 9.497367 9.490038  0.007328946 2008.50
#> 200: 9.483562 9.492102 -0.008539432 2008.75
#> 201: 9.466950 9.494061 -0.027110867 2009.00
#> 202: 9.465099 9.495969 -0.030869902 2009.25
#> 203: 9.471961 9.497861 -0.025899315 2009.50
attr(x = hp, which = "lambda")
#> [1] 1600
